user.title: Connect FeiNiu Music
user.description: Use a regular music account; no NAS administrator account is needed. Copy the full FeiNiu Music page address from your browser, for example http://test:5666/music/ (replace test with your NAS address). Keep the actual port: a default installation usually uses 5666. Custom ports, HTTPS reverse proxies and server root URLs are also supported.

reauth_confirm.title: Update music password
reauth_confirm.description: Enter the password for the existing music account. Leave blank to keep the saved password. To change server or username, remove this source and add it again.

reconfigure.title: Update music password
reconfigure.description: The server and username are fixed for this source. Leave blank to keep the saved password. To change server or username, remove this source and add it again.

outputs.title: Select queue outputs
outputs.description: Create a FeiNiu player for each speaker already connected to HA. The list filters for loading specified media (PLAY_MEDIA); play/pause or volume control alone is insufficient. Outputs must also reach HA audio URLs and decode the format; appearing here does not guarantee playback. Saved offline bindings can be retained. Different protocol entities for one speaker may conflict. Leave empty to use only the media source.

playback.title: Playback feedback and continuation
playback.description: Each FeiNiu player has independent start and end detection settings. Other outputs are unaffected. The music card is not required.

playback_profile.title: Playback feedback and continuation
playback_profile.description:
**{player}**

`{entity_id}`

These preferences apply only to this player. Saving does not restart playback or clear its queue. Feedback mode and estimated continuation take effect on the next playback round; other preferences still take effect immediately.

data.play_once: Send one extra Play after loading
data.weak_end: Allow end-state transition continuation after confirmed playback

data_description.feedback_mode: Standard ends the round and revokes its stream on confirmation timeout; buffered audio may continue. Compatibility keeps the round when the play request succeeds but startup feedback is delayed or missing. This does not verify audible playback. Controls from other apps or speaker buttons may not stay in sync. Compatibility offers estimated continuation in the next step.
data_description.confirmation: Both choices require current-media association and a playing report. The default also requires delivery for this round or at least two valid fresh position samples. Software feedback does not prove audible playback. Use reported-only confirmation only with reliable output feedback.
data_description.end_state: Only applies to confirmed playback transitioning from playing to this state. Default completion checks also require matching media and native progress near the end. Paused or off may instead reflect a user action.
data_description.play_once: Send at most one extra Play while this round is unconfirmed, only if its media matches and the output supports PLAY. This does not loop or retry.
data_description.weak_end: Only applies after startup has been confirmed. May mistake manual pause or stop for completion. Does not enable duration-based continuation for unconfirmed playback.

unconfirmed_end.title: Playback feedback and continuation
unconfirmed_end.description: Off by default. Requires a successful play request, first-byte delivery for this round and a valid duration. The monotonic clock starts at the later of command return and first-byte delivery; continuation waits the track duration plus 5 seconds. Delayed starts, buffering, inaccurate durations or unreported external pauses may cause early or late changes. Delivery is not proof of sound. Takes effect on the next playback round.

data.estimated: Advance by estimated duration when playback is unconfirmed
